propositions: The byte-equivalence test oracle invokes Pandoc twice per unit (884 subprocesses total) with both production and copied legacy implementations sharing live _PANDOC_TO constants, defeating independent validation and causing mutation of one to silently pass both.

Replacing the copied legacy subprocess with an immutable golden fixture preserves all 884 real production Pandoc calls while eliminating the 884 redundant legacy subprocesses and reducing oracle runtime from 65.5s to 33.1s (49.4%).

The fixture schema must store the exact generating Pandoc version and platform-specific binary SHA-256 fingerprints (darwin-arm64 and linux-x86_64), selecting the current platform's hash at validation time to reject version/platform mismatches.

Patchset-1 CI failed all Ubuntu jobs because the schema stored only a single macOS-arm64 binary fingerprint and rejected the identical Pandoc 3.6.1 Linux x86_64 build by differing SHA-256, proving the single-platform design violated the platform-independent contract.
